subject: Recap + clarifications: SpectraHealth evaluation workflow & scoring
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa.gomez@spectrahealth.com>, Dr. Kamal Rao <kamal.rao@spectrahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + clarifications: SpectraHealth evaluation workflow & scoring

Hi Alyssa / Kamal —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can get your evaluation running on Redwood next week. High-level next steps we agreed to: 

- Redwood provides a lightweight eval harness you can run or we can run in a private project (you preferred Redwood-run to start).
- You’ll share a 1–2k sample of de-identified prompts + expected outputs (CSV manifest).
- We’ll run 3 candidate model configs, return tokenized generations, automatic metrics (ROUGE/BLEU/EM depending on task), and a human review pass for edge-case scoring.
- Decide on latency/throughput SLOs and acceptable quality thresholds for replacement.

Clarifying Qs from our side: 
1) Primary task type: is this clinical summarization (condense encounter notes) or triage classification? You mentioned both — which one is the primary axis for this eval?
2) Data format: will the CSV have two columns (prompt, reference) or multiple columns (patient_metadata, note_text, reference)? We usually prefer prompt + reference + id columns.
3) Human labelers: will Spectra provide the final human-review batch or do you want us to coordinate a small 200-example crowd review?

I attached a small manifest example and our eval template. I also attached the model recommendation PDF we discussed (rough picks: Redwood-13B-quant-fast, Llama-3-13B-std, and a smaller 7B for latency baselines).

If you can reply with answers to Q1–Q3, we’ll lock the schedule and I’ll have Marissa (score lead) draft the rubric.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: spectr a_sample_manifest.csv (stub), redwood_eval_template_v1.zip (stub), model_recommendations_0526.pdf (stub)

Subject: Re: Recap + clarifications: SpectraHealth evaluation workflow & scoring

Thanks Ben — useful summary. Quick answers below: 

Hi team,

1) Primary task: clinical summarization of patient encounter notes into a single-paragraph clinician summary. Triage classification is a secondary project.
2) Data format: we can provide CSV with columns: id, encounter_text, reference_summary, patient_age_bucket. We can drop PHI; IT will scrub identifiers.
3) Human labels: Spectra will provide an internal clinician review panel for the final 200 examples, but we’d like Redwood to run the automated scoring + prepare the human review UI/export.

A couple of asks from our side: 
- Can you confirm tokenization details and the maximum prompt + context length you’ll use for the 13B runs? We need to ensure we don’t exceed our scrubbed note size.
- For the rubric, we want a clinical-fidelity weight (70%) and readability weight (30%). Any chance you can bake that into the initial scoring?

Proposed timeline: share sample CSV by Tue 6/1 EOD, Redwood-run tests 6/2–6/4, human review week of 6/7.

Best,
Alyssa
Sr. PM, Clinical AI
SpectraHealth

Perfect — thanks Alyssa. Short answers and what we’re sending you now: 

- Tokenization / context: for the 13B config we’ll use a 4096-token context window; we’ll truncate to the last 3500 tokens of the encounter_text and include patient metadata in the prompt header. We’ll include token counts in the output CSV so you can verify.
- Rubric: yes — we’ll calculate a weighted score (0–100) composed of clinical_fidelity*0.7 + readability*0.3. We’ll return component scores plus a composite metric and a small failure-mode tagset (hallucination, truncation, omissions).

Attached: a filled manifest example (spectra_sample_manifest.csv), the eval harness (redwood_eval_template_v1.zip), and the model recs PDF. 

Next steps (I’ll own):
- Monday 6/1: you drop sample CSV into our secure upload link (I’ll DM the S3 per-request link).
- Tue 6/2: Redwood runs baseline (3 models) and provides automatic metrics + full tokenized outputs.
- Wed 6/3–Thu 6/4: internal quick pass + prepare human review bundle for Spectra’s clinicians.

If that timeline looks good I’ll schedule the run and loop in the infra tech if we need higher throughput.

Subject: Re: Recap + clarifications: SpectraHealth evaluation workflow & scoring

Thanks — quick note from scoring side.

Ben, I drafted an initial rubric and the scoring artifact layout. Key differences we’ll produce in the first pass: 
- Automated metrics: ROUGE-L (for structure), BERTScore (for semantic fidelity), and a custom overlap of clinical entities (ICD-like tags) extracted with our NER model.
- Human review: we’ll create a small Google sheet export with the candidate generation(s), the reference, and three Likert questions: Clinical Accuracy (1–5), Missing Core Info (1–5, reverse), Readability (1–5). We’ll map these back to the 0–100 composite.
- Edge-case sampling: we’ll stratify the 200 human-review items by complexity (short notes, long notes, multi-problem encounters).

Two asks for Spectra: 
1) Please confirm whether patient_age_bucket is required for the scorer or just for stratification. If not required, we’ll ignore for scoring and only use for split analysis.
2) If you have any specific entity tags (e.g., medication changes, discharge errors) please share the short list so we can tune the NER overlap.

Alyssa, once you upload the sample CSV Ben mentioned, I’ll generate the initial metric run and share the dashboard link.

—Marissa
Head of Evaluations
Redwood Inference

Small technical note from runtime side that affects the 13B vs 7B baselines and your latency expectations: 

- The 13B-quant run (our Redwood-13B-quant-fast profile) will deliver steady-state token latency of ~12–18 ms/token under the continuous-batching profile we plan to use. Peak cold-start can be higher for very long context windows because of KV cache sizing (we preallocate for 4k).
- For the 7B config we can hit single-digit ms/token and the cost per token will be ~40% lower — good for a latency-first baseline.
- If Spectra needs strict end-to-end summary latency < 300ms for typical notes, we’ll need to limit generation length or use the 7B baseline; otherwise the 13B run will be higher but with better fidelity in many cases.

Also: confirm whether you want us to retain the raw token outputs in the Redwood project for debugging (we typically keep them for 30 days unless you request longer retention).

I’ll prepare the infra profile for the 6/2 run; Ben — please ping me once the sample CSV is live.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
